# `kernel/navi/NaviPureLocalSpeculation.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/navi/NaviPureLocalSpeculation.js`

A deliberately tiny speculative lane for computation that is stronger than read-only: pure, deterministic, local, authority-free, and data-egress-free. Shadow execution never enters ToolDriver.execute(), ToolRouter, or Faculty. It therefore cannot consume a capability or emit a canonical execution receipt. A result is released only after accept() rebinds the final call and proves that its branch, descriptor, and canonical arguments did not drift.

## Classes

### `class NaviPureLocalShadowExecutor`

Ephemeral executor. Results remain private until accept() validates the final generated call. No method accepts a Faculty grant, capability, or receipt.

## Functions

### `cancelNaviPureLocalAdoption(adoptionToken)`

Retire one exact accepted token when its kernel dispatch cannot reach the router. This is revocation only: unknown, settled, cloned, and replayed tokens return false and can never produce a value or driver-context brand.

### `async bindNaviPureLocalAdoptionAfterFaculty({ adoptionToken, callIdentity, toolDriver, descriptor, args, driverContext, signal = null, } = {})`

Bind an accepted shadow value to the exact live dispatch after ToolRouter has consumed Faculty authorization and repeated its descriptor/input checks. Invalid, replayed, expired, or cancelled tokens simply decline adoption so the caller can execute the ordinary handler through the same canonical path.

### `async consumeNaviPureLocalAdoptionForToolDriver({ driverContext, toolDriver, descriptor, args, signal = null, } = {})`

ToolDriver-only consumption boundary. It independently revalidates the live descriptor and exact arguments before substituting the shadow value. The context brand and adoption state are destroyed before any await can replay them; a failed check returns adopted:false and the normal handler runs.

### `createNaviPureLocalSpeculationContract({ category, descriptorVersion, implementationHash, maxInputBytes = 4096, maxOutputBytes = 4096, maxWallTimeMs = 100, } = {})`

Build the closed attestation required in addition to readOnly:true.

### `assessNaviPureLocalSpeculationEligibility(descriptor)`

Return a content-free eligibility decision. Merely declaring readOnly is categorically insufficient, as network and registry reads still have effects.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
